q.s: Rakhigarhi, regarded as the largest Harappan site in India, is located in which district?
q.x: Rakhigarhi lies in Hisar district of Haryana and is the largest Harappan site; Bhirrana (Fatehabad) is regarded as the oldest.

q.s: Which Harappan site is regarded as the oldest Harappan site?
q.x: Bhirrana in Fatehabad district, Haryana, is regarded as the oldest Harappan site, while Rakhigarhi is the largest.

q.s: The full description of the Upanayana ceremony is found in which text?
q.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana gives the full description of the Upanayana, the thread ceremony performed for the twice-born.

q.s: The Tripitaka consists of the Vinaya, Sutta and which other Pitaka?
q.x: The three baskets are the Vinaya (monastic rules), Sutta (discourses) and Abhidhamma (philosophy) Pitakas.

q.s: The five Nikayas belong to which part of the Buddhist canon?
q.x: The Sutta Pitaka is divided into five Nikayas; the Khuddaka Nikaya among them contains the Jatakas.

q.s: In early Buddhist art, the horse Kanthaka symbolises which event of the Buddha's life?
q.x: The horse Kanthaka stands for the Great Departure; the lotus and bull stand for birth, the empty seat under the Bodhi tree for enlightenment and the wheel for the first sermon.

q.s: In aniconic Buddhist art, the Dharmachakra (wheel) represents:
q.x: The Dharmachakra stands for the Dharmachakrapravartana, the first sermon at Sarnath; the stupa stands for the parinirvana.

q.s: The Buddhist site of Salihundam on the Vamsadhara river is located in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Salihundam is in Srikakulam district; Sankaram is in Anakapalli, Bhairavakonda in Nellore and Guntupalli in West Godavari (Eluru).

q.s: The earliest important works and the first grammar of which language were composed by the Jains?
q.x: Jain writers composed the earliest important works and the first grammar of Apabhramsa; the early Jains preached in Prakrit rather than Sanskrit.

q.s: The manuscript of Kautilya's Arthashastra was identified in 1905 by:
q.x: R. Shamasastry identified the manuscript in 1905 and published it in 1909; the work has 15 books (adhikaranas).

q.s: Kautilya, the author of the Arthashastra, was also known as:
q.x: Kautilya was also called Vishnugupta and Chanakya; Pushyagupta was Chandragupta's governor in Saurashtra.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT usually cited as a cause of the decline of the Mauryan empire?
o: Heavy spending on Dhamma missions and the Sangha
q.x: The Huns invaded much later, in the Gupta period; the other three are standard explanations of the Mauryan decline.

q.s: The 80-pillared hall of Mauryan Pataliputra was found at:
q.x: The 80-pillared hall was excavated at Kumrahar; Bulandibagh yielded the remains of the wooden palisade.

q.s: Chandragupta I married Kumaradevi, a princess of which clan?
q.x: Chandragupta I's marriage to the Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi raised Gupta prestige; Samudragupta is called Lichchhavi-dauhitra.

q.s: The Adhai Din ka Jhonpra at Ajmer was built by:
q.x: Aibak built the Adhai Din ka Jhonpra at Ajmer and began the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque in Delhi.

q.s: In which language did Malik Muhammad Jayasi write the Padmavat (1540)?
q.x: Jayasi wrote the Padmavat in Awadhi in 1540, more than two centuries after Alauddin took Chittor (1303).

q.s: The city of Agra was founded by which dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate?
q.x: Sikandar Lodi founded Agra; the Lodis were also the first Afghan dynasty of the Sultanate.

q.s: The Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi is:
q.x: The Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi is Firoz's own account of his reign; the Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi is a Persian translation of Sanskrit manuscripts from Nagarkot.

q.s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq's expeditions to Bengal were directed against:
q.x: Firoz led two unsuccessful expeditions to Bengal against Haji Iliyas; Jam Babaniya of Sind agreed to pay tribute.

q.s: Which was the first Afghan dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate?
q.x: The Lodi dynasty founded by Bahlol Lodi (1451) was the first Afghan dynasty; Sikandar and Ibrahim followed.

q.s: The city of Siri, the second city of Delhi, was built by:
q.x: Siri was built by Alauddin Khalji; Tughlaqabad by Ghiyasuddin, Jahanpanah by Muhammad bin Tughlaq and Hisar by Firoz.

q.s: The Diwan-i-Kohi, a department of agriculture, was set up by:
q.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq created the Diwan-i-Kohi to extend cultivation.

q.s: The Diwan-i-Insha of the Delhi Sultanate dealt with:
q.x: The Diwan-i-Insha, headed by the Dabir-i-Khas, handled royal correspondence; religious affairs came under the Diwan-i-Risalat.

q.s: Which Sultan ran about 36 royal karkhanas?
q.x: Firoz Tughlaq maintained about 36 royal karkhanas supplying the court.

q.s: The Chishti saints spoke to the common people in which language?
q.x: The Chishtis used Hindavi to reach ordinary people, an important aspect of syncretism in the Sultanate period.

q.s: Akbar was enthroned in 1556 at:
q.x: Akbar was crowned at Kalanaur (Punjab) on 14 February 1556; he had been born at Amarkot in 1542.

q.s: The 'petticoat government' in Akbar's early reign refers to the dominance of:
q.x: The petticoat government (1560-64) was the influence of Akbar's foster-mother Maham Anaga and her son Adham Khan.

q.s: Guru Gobind Singh wrote the Zafarnama to which Mughal emperor?
q.x: After the battle of Chamkaur (1704), Guru Gobind Singh wrote the Zafarnama rebuking Aurangzeb for broken oaths of safe passage.

q.s: Baisakhi is celebrated by the Sikhs as the foundation day of:
o: The Sikh kingdom of Ranjit Singh
q.x: Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa on Baisakhi day in 1699.

q.s: Who was the guru of Kabir?
q.x: By tradition Ramananda was Kabir's guru; Vallabhacharya was Surdas's guru and Ravidas was Mirabai's.

q.s: Surdas was a disciple of:
q.x: Surdas belonged to the Pushti Marga of Vallabhacharya.

q.s: Ramanuja is credited with installing which deity at Tirupati?
q.x: Ramanuja is credited with installing Govindaraja at Tirupati; he also inspired Palnati Brahmanaidu's Veera Vaishnava movement.

q.s: During Dutch rule, Pulicat was an important centre of:
q.x: Pulicat, the Dutch headquarters on the Coromandel coast, was a hub of the slave trade to Batavia; Koringa was known for shipbuilding.

q.s: The first Danish settlement in India (1620) was at:
q.x: Tranquebar (Tharangambadi) near Tanjore was the first Danish settlement; Serampore and Tranquebar were sold to the British in 1845.

q.s: The Ostend Company, chartered in 1722, belonged to:
q.x: The Ostend Company of the Austrian Netherlands had settlements at Banquibazar in Bengal and Covelong near Madras.

q.s: The first relief of Lucknow in September 1857 was carried out by:
q.x: Havelock and Outram made the first relief (25 September 1857); Colin Campbell made the second relief and recaptured Lucknow in March 1858.

q.s: Who described the revolt of 1857 as "in truth a national revolt" in the New-York Tribune?
q.x: Karl Marx wrote on the revolt for the New-York Tribune; Disraeli raised the question of mutiny or national revolt in the Commons.

q.s: Who was the first Secretary of State for India under the Government of India Act, 1858?
q.x: Lord Stanley became the first Secretary of State for India; Canning became the first Viceroy.

q.s: Who became the first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833?
q.x: The Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India, and Bentinck was the first.

q.s: Which ruler of Mysore became 'Citizen Tipu' through a Jacobin Club founded at Seringapatam in 1797?
q.x: Tipu Sultan backed the Jacobin Club at Seringapatam; he also set up a Board of Admiralty and pioneered war rockets.

q.s: The Ulgulan (Great Tumult) of 1899-1900 was led by:
q.x: Birsa Munda proclaimed the Ulgulan on Christmas Eve 1899 aiming at Abua Raj (self-rule).

q.s: Who was the first and the last Indian Governor-General of India?
q.x: C. Rajagopalachari succeeded Mountbatten in 1948 and was the only Indian Governor-General.

q.s: The Board of Control to supervise the East India Company was created by:
q.x: Pitt's India Act of 1784 created the Board of Control; the 1813 Act ended the Company's trade monopoly except in tea and the China trade.

q.s: Which Act ended the East India Company's monopoly of Indian trade, except in tea and trade with China?
q.x: The 1813 Act ended the trade monopoly (except tea and China trade) and allowed missionaries into India.

q.s: The Guntur famine known as 'Dokkala Karuvu' or 'Nandana Karuvu' occurred in:
q.x: The Guntur famine of 1832-33 is remembered as Dokkala or Nandana Karuvu; the Great Famine came in 1876-78.

q.s: 'Vanguard', regarded as the first communist paper of India, was associated with:
q.x: Vanguard was M.N. Roy's journal; The Socialist was edited by S.A. Dange and the Labour Kisan Gazette by Singaravelu.

q.s: What was the original name of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa?
q.x: Ramakrishna was born Gadadhar Chattopadhyay; Narendranath Datta was Vivekananda's name.

q.s: Ramakrishna Paramahamsa served as a priest at the Kali temple at:
q.x: He was a priest at the Dakshineswar Kali temple; Belur Math was founded later by Vivekananda.

q.s: The paper 'Bande Mataram' was published from Paris by:
q.x: Madame Bhikaji Cama published Bande Mataram from Paris; Taraknath Das published Free Hindustan.

q.s: The newspaper 'Comrade' was edited by:
q.x: Muhammad Ali published the English weekly Comrade; Azad's paper was Al-Hilal.

q.s: The Surat split of 1907 was healed and the Extremists readmitted at which session of the Congress?
q.x: The Moderates and Extremists reunited at the Lucknow session of 1916 presided over by A.C. Majumdar.

q.s: At which session of the Muslim League did Muhammad Iqbal propose a North-West Indian Muslim state in 1930?
q.x: Iqbal made the proposal in his presidential address at the Allahabad session of 1930.

q.s: The Muslim League observed 'Direct Action Day' on:
q.x: Direct Action Day, 16 August 1946, led to the Great Calcutta Killings; 22 December 1939 was the Day of Deliverance.

q.s: Who was the president of the Andhra branch of the Swaraj Party?
q.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was the president and Unnava Lakshminarayana the secretary of the Andhra Swaraj Party.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT agreed to by Lord Irwin under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931)?
o: Release of political prisoners not convicted of violence
Coastal villagers making salt for their own use
A public inquiry into police excesses
Withdrawal of ordinances issued during the movement
q.x: Irwin refused a public inquiry into police excesses; the pact did not save Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru either.

q.s: The Ramgarh session of the Indian National Congress (1940) was presided over by:
q.x: Maulana Azad presided over the Ramgarh session of March 1940, held before the August Offer.

q.s: Matangini Hazra, a martyr of the Quit India Movement, was shot while leading a procession at:
q.x: Matangini Hazra, aged 73, was shot at Tamluk (Midnapore); Kanaklata Barua was shot at Gohpur in Assam.

q.s: The League raised the slogan 'Divide and Quit' at which of its sessions?
q.x: The slogan 'Divide and Quit' was given at the Karachi session of December 1943.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The C.R. Formula was proposed by Chittaranjan Das.
The Desai-Liaquat Pact gave the Congress a majority in the interim government.
The C.R. Formula was accepted by the Muslim League in 1944.
q.x: C. Rajagopalachari's formula of 1944 offered a post-war plebiscite in Muslim-majority areas, but Jinnah rejected it; the Desai-Liaquat Pact proposed equal Congress and League nominees.

q.s: Which prison did Gandhi call his 'Mandir'?
q.x: Gandhi called Yerawada Jail (Pune) his 'Mandir'; Tilak and Bose were held at Mandalay.

q.s: The Sadaqat Ashram, associated with Gandhi's work in Bihar, is located at:
q.x: Sadaqat Ashram at Patna became the headquarters of the Bihar Congress.

q.s: In 1920 Gandhi returned which award as part of the Non-Cooperation protest?
q.x: Gandhi returned his Kaisar-i-Hind medal in 1920 when he launched the Khilafat-Non-Cooperation Movement; it was Tagore who returned his knighthood in 1919.

q.s: Which of the following princely states had NOT acceded to India by 15 August 1947?
q.x: Junagadh, Hyderabad and Kashmir were the hold-outs on 15 August 1947; Bhopal, Travancore and Jodhpur had acceded.

q.s: The Instrument of Accession of 1947 ceded which subjects to the Centre?
q.x: Princely states acceded on the three subjects of Defence, External Affairs and Communications.

q.s: Chandernagore, a former French settlement, was merged into which state?
q.x: Chandernagore merged into West Bengal; Pondicherry, Karikal, Mahe and Yanam form the Union Territory of Puducherry.

q.s: Yanam, a part of Puducherry UT, lies in the delta of which river?
q.x: Yanam is an enclave in the Godavari delta, surrounded by Andhra Pradesh's East Godavari region.

q.s: Who presided over the first Andhra Conference held at Bapatla in 1913?
q.x: B.N. Sarma presided at Bapatla but felt the demand for a separate province premature.

q.s: The Hathigumpha inscription belongs to which ruler?
q.x: The Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela of Kalinga mentions Satakarni and the river Kanhabenna (Krishna).

q.s: Which sources describe the Satavahanas as 'Andhras' or 'Andhrabhrityas'?
q.x: The Puranas call the Satavahanas Andhras or Andhrabhrityas; Ashoka's 13th Rock Edict lists the Andhras among his subject peoples.

q.s: Rudradaman's victory over the Satavahana Satakarni is recorded in which inscription?
q.x: The Junagadh (Girnar) inscription says Rudradaman twice defeated Satakarni but spared him as a near relative.

q.s: In the Satavahana period, the Palnadu region was associated with:
q.x: Palnadu was known for diamonds; Guduru for fine cotton and Vinukonda for metal.

q.s: Among the samantas of the Satavahanas, the Ikshvakus had their seat at:
q.x: The Ikshvakus, feudatories of the Satavahanas, ruled from Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda); the Chutus were in Mysore and the Kuras at Kolhapur.

q.s: In the Satavahana period, the head of a guild (shreni) was called:
q.x: A guild was headed by a Shreshthi (Setti); guilds fixed quality and prices and later hardened into castes.

q.s: The rock-cut chaitya at Karle is famous for its sculptures of:
q.x: Karle's chaitya has sculptured dance couples; the Ajanta Cave 10 painting shows the Chhaddanta Jataka and Nasik has viharas with Satavahana inscriptions.

q.s: Sultan Quli, the founder of the Qutb Shahi kingdom of Golconda, was earlier the Bahmani governor (tarafdar) of:
q.x: Sultan Quli was the Bahmani tarafdar of Telangana before founding the Qutb Shahi state; the Bahmani kingdom broke up after Mahmud Gawan's execution in 1482.

q.s: The novel 'Karpura Vasanta Rayalu' by C. Narayana Reddy is about which Reddi ruler?
q.x: Karpura Vasanta Rayalu celebrates Kumaragiri Reddi, whose court held the Vasantotsavam and had the dancer Lakumadevi.

q.s: Kollur, the diamond mine often cited as the source of the Kohinoor, lies on the Krishna river in which district?
q.x: Kollur is on the Krishna in Guntur district; Vajra Karur is in Anantapur and Ramalla Kota in Kurnool.

q.s: Under Abul Hasan Tana Shah of Golconda, who was the Mir Jumla (prime minister)?
q.x: Madanna was prime minister and his brother Akkanna the army chief; Kancherla Gopanna (Bhakta Ramadasu) was their nephew.

q.s: Achyutaraya of Vijayanagara belonged to which dynasty?
q.x: Achyutaraya was a Tuluva, the half-brother and successor of Krishnadevaraya.

q.s: The last Sangama ruler, Praudha Raya, was overthrown in 1485 by:
q.x: Saluva Narasimha ended the Sangama dynasty in 1485 and founded the Saluva dynasty.

q.s: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam records the capture of Motupalli by:
q.x: Devaraya I's capture of southern Kondaveedu including Motupalli is recorded in the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam.

q.s: In the Vijayanagara judicial system, civil cases were called:
q.x: Dhanodbhava cases were civil and Himsodbhava cases criminal; treason was punished with death.

q.s: After the weakening of Vijayanagara, the amara-nayakas became hereditary chiefs known as:
q.x: The amara-nayakas turned into hereditary Palegars (poligars), forerunners of the later zamindars.

q.s: The Vilasa grant of the Musunuri Nayaks was issued by:
q.x: Prolaya Nayaka issued the Vilasa grant, which describes the Musunuri liberation of Andhra.

q.s: 'Sangeeta Sudhakaram', a commentary on Sarngadeva's Sangita Ratnakara, was written by:
q.x: Sarvagna Singabhupala II of Rachakonda wrote Sangeeta Sudhakaram on the Sangita Ratnakara.

q.s: The Lepakshi temple was built under Achyutaraya by governors of:
q.x: Virupanna and Veeranna, governors of Penukonda, built Lepakshi c. 1530-40; it is in Sri Sathya Sai district.

q.s: Which was the first capital of the Aravidu dynasty after the battle of Talikota?
q.x: The Aravidus moved first to Penukonda (1570), then Chandragiri and later Vellore (1600).

q.s: The idols of Gandikota were looted in 1657 by:
q.x: Mir Jumla, the Golconda general, took Gandikota and looted its idols.

q.s: The Venetian traveller Marco Polo visited the port of Motupalli in 1287 during the reign of:
q.x: Marco Polo visited Motupalli under Rudrama Devi; Ganapatideva's Abhaya Sasanam had earlier protected foreign traders there.

q.s: Who was the Principal Collector of the Ceded Districts who suppressed the palegars?
q.x: Thomas Munro put down about 80 palegars and introduced the Ryotwari system in the Ceded Districts.

q.s: The Ceded Districts (Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur, Bellary) were ceded to the Company in 1800 by:
q.x: The Nizam ceded these districts under the Subsidiary Alliance to pay for the subsidiary force.

q.s: Why did Andhra largely stay loyal to the British during the Revolt of 1857?
o: The Company had abolished the zamindari system
People valued the Company's stable government over earlier anarchy
q.x: Many preferred the Company's stable rule to the earlier disorder, and the Nizam's loyalty kept the Deccan quiet.

q.s: Which Andhra writer wrote 'Japan Charitra', a history of Japan in Telugu, after Japan's victory over Russia in 1905?
q.x: Adipudi Somanatha Rao wrote Japan Charitra; Sriram Veerabrahmam wrote the drama Japaniyam.

q.s: In 1938, students of which university, including P.V. Narasimha Rao, were expelled for singing Vande Mataram?
q.x: The Vande Mataram agitation of 1938 led to the expulsion of Osmania University students including P.V. Narasimha Rao.

q.s: The Sirimanu utsavam of Paidithalli Ammavaru is celebrated at:
q.x: The Paidithalli Ammavaru festival with its Sirimanu utsavam is held at Vizianagaram; the Gangamma Jatara is at Tirupati.

q.s: The Gangamma Jatara is a famous festival of:
q.x: The week-long Gangamma Jatara is celebrated at Tirupati; Kotappakonda is known for its Shivaratri tirunallu.

q.s: The Undavalli Caves, a rock-cut monument of Andhra Pradesh, are located on the bank of which river?
q.x: The Undavalli Caves stand on the south bank of the Krishna opposite Vijayawada, in Guntur district.

q.s: The Talagunda inscription describes the founding of which kingdom?
q.x: The Talagunda inscription narrates how Mayurasharman founded the Kadamba kingdom.

q.s: The Mayidavolu plates of Sivaskandavarman are written in which language?
q.x: The Mayidavolu plates, issued by Sivaskandavarman as yuvaraja, are among the earliest Pallava records and are in Prakrit.

q.s: The Satyashodhak form of marriage, without dowry and without a Brahmin priest, was started by:
q.x: The Satyashodhak marriage was promoted by the Phules' Satyashodhak Samaj; it dispensed with dowry and Brahmin priests.

q.s: The relationship between a man and his sister's daughter is an example of:
q.x: Ties of blood are consanguineous; ties through marriage, such as husband-wife or brothers-in-law, are affinal.

q.s: The Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 was renamed in 1976 as the:
o: SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
q.x: It became the Protection of Civil Rights Act in 1976; the Atrocities Act is a separate law of 1989.

q.s: 'Inclusive growth' was the central aim of which Five Year Plan?
q.x: The Eleventh Plan (2007-12) was titled 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth'; the Twelfth added 'sustainable'.

q.s: According to Census 2011, which is the largest tribe of India?
q.x: The Bhil is the largest tribe and the Gond the second-largest; Madhya Pradesh has the largest ST population by number.

q.s: According to Census 2011, which State has the largest Scheduled Tribe population by number?
q.x: Madhya Pradesh has the largest ST population; Mizoram has the highest ST share among States.

q.s: The Anti-Arrack Movement of Andhra Pradesh began in 1992 at Dubagunta in which district?
q.x: The movement started at Dubagunta in Nellore district and led to a ban on arrack in 1993.

q.s: In which case did a seven-judge Bench of the Supreme Court allow sub-classification of Scheduled Castes in 2024?
o: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh
E.V. Chinnaiah v. State of A.P.
M. Nagaraj v. Union of India
q.x: Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024), by 6:1, allowed sub-classification and overruled E.V. Chinnaiah (2004).

q.s: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) was constituted under the:
o: Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
q.x: The NCPCR is a statutory body under the 2005 Act; it monitors the POCSO, JJ and RTE Acts.

q.s: The National Child Labour Project (NCLP) is implemented by which Ministry?
q.x: The NCLP, started in 1988, is run by the Ministry of Labour and Employment for rescued children aged 9-14.

q.s: The National Service Scheme (NSS), started in 1969, has the motto idea of:
q.x: NSS was launched in 1969 on the idea of 'Education through Service' (motto 'Not Me But You').

q.s: The Dalit Panthers, a militant Dalit youth organisation, were formed in 1972 in:
q.x: The Dalit Panthers were founded in Bombay in 1972 by Namdeo Dhasal, J.V. Pawar and others.

q.s: According to NITI Aayog's National MPI 2023 (NFHS-5 data), which State had the highest multidimensional poverty headcount?
q.x: Bihar recorded the highest headcount (33.76%); India's figure was 14.96%.

q.s: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao falls under which vertical of Mission Shakti?
q.x: Mission Shakti has two verticals: Sambal (safety, including BBBP and One Stop Centres) and Samarthya (empowerment).

q.s: Tithi Bhojan, community participation in the mid-day meal, was first introduced by:
q.x: Gujarat pioneered Tithi Bhojan; Andhra Pradesh's mid-day meal scheme is named after Dokka Seethamma.

q.s: Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, Child Marriage Prohibition Officers are appointed by:
q.x: The State Government appoints Child Marriage Prohibition Officers; the Act treats marriage below 18 (girls) and 21 (boys) as child marriage.

q.s: 'Nai Roshni', a scheme of the Ministry of Minority Affairs, is meant for:
o: Education and skills for school dropouts
q.x: Nai Roshni (2013) trains minority women in leadership; USTTAD supports traditional arts and Nai Manzil serves dropouts.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution gives any section of citizens the right to conserve its distinct language, script or culture?
q.x: Article 29(1) is available to any section of citizens, including the majority; Article 30 is only for minorities.

q.s: The grouping I2U2, called the 'West Asia Quad', consists of India, Israel, the USA and:
q.x: I2U2 comprises India, Israel, the UAE and the USA.

q.s: Which India-US foundational agreement concerns the sharing of geospatial intelligence?
q.x: BECA (2020) covers geospatial intelligence; COMCASA covers encrypted communications, LEMOA logistics and GSOMIA military information security.

q.s: The India-US civil nuclear cooperation agreement of 2008 is popularly known as the:
q.x: The 2008 deal is the 123 Agreement, named after Section 123 of the US Atomic Energy Act; the Hyde Act of 2006 enabled it.

q.s: Kovvada, the proposed site for nuclear reactors in Andhra Pradesh, is in which district?
q.x: Kovvada is in Srikakulam district on the north coastal belt.

q.s: Which GATT Article permits free trade agreements as exceptions to the MFN principle?
q.x: Article XXIV allows FTAs and customs unions covering substantially all trade; Article XX contains general exceptions.

q.s: The Council of Europe is headquartered at:
q.x: The Council of Europe (1949) is based at Strasbourg and is separate from the European Union.

q.s: Which export control regime deals with chemical and biological weapons-related items?
q.x: The Australia Group controls chemical and biological items; the MTCR covers missiles and drones carrying 500 kg over 300 km.

q.s: The Wassenaar Arrangement on conventional arms and dual-use goods is based at:
q.x: The Wassenaar Arrangement (1996) has its secretariat at Vienna.

q.s: The idea of nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha was borrowed from the Constitution of:
q.x: Nomination to the Rajya Sabha came from Ireland, as did the Directive Principles; impeachment of the President came from the USA.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution empowers Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law?
q.x: Article 11 lets Parliament regulate acquisition and termination of citizenship; Article 9 deals with voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship.

q.s: The Six-Point Formula for Andhra Pradesh was given constitutional backing through:
q.x: The 32nd Amendment (1973) inserted Article 371D; Article 371E provides for a central university in Andhra Pradesh.

q.s: The first spell of President's Rule in Andhra Pradesh (1973) followed which agitation?
q.x: The Jai Andhra agitation led to President's Rule from January to December 1973, ending when Jalagam Vengala Rao became Chief Minister.

q.s: The Mandal Commission estimated the OBC population of India at about:
q.x: The Mandal Commission put OBCs at 52 per cent and recommended 27 per cent reservation; it listed 3,743 backward castes.

q.s: Which Constitutional Amendment abolished the privy purses of former rulers?
q.x: The 26th Amendment (1971) abolished privy purses; the 25th inserted Article 31C.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that students cannot be compelled to sing the National Anthem?
q.x: Bijoe Emmanuel (1986) held that standing respectfully suffices and duties cannot override fundamental rights.

q.s: The phrase 'procedure established by law' in Article 21 was borrowed from the Constitution of:
q.x: 'Procedure established by law' came from Japan; the doctrine of pith and substance from Canada.

q.s: The doctrine of prospective overruling was first applied in India in which case?
q.x: The Supreme Court first applied prospective overruling, a doctrine of US origin, in Golaknath (1967).

q.s: Laws made under Articles 2 and 3 for the formation of new States amend which Schedules of the Constitution?
q.x: They amend the First (States and territories) and Fourth (Rajya Sabha seats) Schedules and are not treated as amendments under Article 368.

q.s: In which year was Andhra State formed?
q.x: Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953; Andhra Pradesh followed on 1 November 1956.

q.s: Sikkim became the 22nd State of India by which Constitutional Amendment?
q.x: The 35th Amendment (1974) made Sikkim an associate State and the 36th (1975) a full State.

q.s: To whom does the Speaker of the Lok Sabha address the resignation?
q.x: The Speaker resigns by writing to the Deputy Speaker; a Governor resigns to the President.

q.s: Who was the first non-Congress Prime Minister of India?
q.x: Morarji Desai of the Janata Party became PM in 1977; Gulzarilal Nanda was twice acting PM.

q.s: Which Prime Minister never faced the Lok Sabha during his tenure?
q.x: Charan Singh (1979-80) resigned before facing the Lok Sabha.

q.s: The population base used for the value of votes in the Presidential election has been frozen at which Census?
q.x: The 1971 Census is used, frozen by the 84th Amendment until the first Census after 2026.

q.s: The 99th Constitutional Amendment and the NJAC Act were struck down in:
q.x: The SC Advocates-on-Record Association case (2015) struck down the NJAC and restored the collegium.

q.s: Which Supreme Court case laid down guidelines on sexual harassment of women at the workplace?
q.x: Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997) laid down the guidelines; Prakash Singh (2006) dealt with police reforms.

q.s: The right to privacy was declared a fundamental right in:
q.x: A nine-judge Bench in Puttaswamy (2017) held privacy to be part of Article 21.

q.s: Which of the following countries has a unitary form of government?
q.x: Sri Lanka is a unitary state; Switzerland, the USA and Australia are federations.

q.s: The Zonal Councils were set up under:
q.x: Zonal Councils are statutory bodies under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, proposed by Nehru.

q.s: Which Constitutional Amendment made all Union taxes shareable with the States through a divisible pool?
q.x: The 80th Amendment (2000) adopted the Tenth Finance Commission's alternative scheme of devolution; surcharges and cesses stay outside the pool.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the removal and suspension of members of a Public Service Commission?
q.x: Article 317 covers removal and suspension; 316 deals with appointment and term and 320 with functions.

q.s: The Comptroller and Auditor General holds office for six years or till the age of:
q.x: Under the CAG Act, 1971 the CAG serves six years or till 65, whichever is earlier.

q.s: Which Constitutional Amendment raised the retirement age of High Court judges from 60 to 62?
q.x: The 15th Amendment (1963) raised the retirement age of High Court judges to 62.

q.s: The first report of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission dealt with:
q.x: The first report (2006) was 'Right to Information: Master Key to Good Governance'; the fourth was 'Ethics in Governance'.

q.s: The Law Commission of India is:
o: A non-statutory body set up by executive order
A statutory body under an Act of 1955
A body under the Supreme Court
q.x: The Law Commission is constituted by executive order for three years and reports to the Ministry of Law and Justice.

q.s: Who was the first State Chief Information Commissioner of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: C.D. Arha was the first; Jannat Hussain the second.

q.s: The Lokayukta of Andhra Pradesh, set up under the 1983 Act, submits its reports to:
q.x: The AP Lokayukta is a statutory ombudsman reporting to the Governor.

q.s: Which section of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 requires every State to establish a Lokayukta within one year?
q.x: Section 63 obliged every State to set up a Lokayukta by its own law within a year of commencement.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the selection committee for the Lokpal?
q.x: The committee comprises the PM, the Speaker, the Leader of Opposition, the CJI (or a nominee) and an eminent jurist.

q.s: What minimum proportion of Lokpal members must be judicial members?
q.x: At least half the members must be judicial; the Lokpal has a Chairperson and up to 8 members.

q.s: Under which Article does the Governor hold office during the pleasure of the President?
q.x: Article 156(1) makes the Governor's tenure subject to the President's pleasure; Article 155 deals with appointment.

q.s: A State's original suit against the Union, such as Kerala's suit on borrowing limits, is filed under:
q.x: Article 131 gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction in disputes between the Union and the States; borrowing by States is governed by Article 293.

q.s: The Standing Committee of the Inter-State Council is chaired by:
q.x: The Standing Committee (1996) is chaired by the Union Home Minister; the Council itself is chaired by the Prime Minister.

q.s: Mallikarjun Kharge became President of the Indian National Congress in:
q.x: Kharge was elected INC president in October 2022, defeating Shashi Tharoor.

q.s: How many Lok Sabha seats did the BJP win in the 2014 general election?
q.x: The BJP won 282 seats in 2014, the first single-party majority since 1984; it won 240 in 2024.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of democratic decentralisation?
o: Concentration of power in the State capital
q.x: Democratic decentralisation means autonomy, participation and empowerment; political decentralisation transfers the power to decide to elected local bodies.

q.s: The main own-source revenue of a Gram Panchayat is:
q.x: House or property tax is the chief own revenue of Gram Panchayats; the higher tiers depend mainly on grants.

q.s: Nehru's 'Panchsheel' for tribal development was set out in his foreword to which book?
o: The Tribal World of Verrier Elwin
q.x: Nehru wrote the tribal Panchsheel in his foreword to Verrier Elwin's 'A Philosophy for NEFA'.

q.s: PM-JANMAN, launched in November 2023, is meant for:
q.x: PM-JANMAN targets the 75 PVTGs; the Dharti Aaba Abhiyan is run by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.

q.s: The National Awards for e-Governance are instituted by DARPG together with:
q.x: DARPG gives the awards along with the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology; they began in 2003.

q.s: Aadhaar serves as a proof of:
q.x: Aadhaar, issued by UIDAI under the Aadhaar Act, 2016, is not proof of citizenship.

q.s: Digital India, launched on 1 July 2015, rests on how many pillars?
q.x: Digital India has nine pillars, from Broadband Highways to Early Harvest Programmes, coordinated by MeitY.

q.s: Eco Mark for environment-friendly products is issued by:
q.x: Eco Mark (1991) is awarded by the BIS; Agmark for agricultural produce dates from 1937.

q.s: The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 was replaced by:
q.x: The FSS Act, 2006 replaced the PFA Act and set up FSSAI.

q.s: Where was the 14th Summit of the Non-Aligned Movement held?
q.x: The 14th Summit (2006) was at Havana; Kuala Lumpur hosted the 13th and Sharm el-Sheikh the 15th.

q.s: How many Afro-Asian countries attended the Bandung Conference of April 1955?
q.x: Twenty-nine countries attended Bandung, a precursor of the Non-Aligned Movement.

q.s: Which State topped both editions of NITI Aayog's Composite Water Management Index?
q.x: Gujarat ranked first in CWMI 2018 and CWMI 2.0 (2019); Andhra Pradesh was third and then second.

q.s: The Mihir Shah Committee (2016) recommended merging the CWC and CGWB into a:
q.x: The Mihir Shah Committee proposed a National Water Commission; the Ground Water Quality Report is brought out by the CGWB.

q.s: The WTO dispute DS456 brought by the USA against India related to:
q.x: India lost DS456 (2016) on domestic content requirements under the National Solar Mission.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT covered by the GATT but is covered by the WTO?
q.x: The GATT dealt mainly with goods; the WTO also covers services (GATS), IPRs (TRIPS) and investment measures (TRIMs).

q.s: The Planetary pressures-adjusted HDI (PHDI) adjusts the HDI for:
q.x: The PHDI discounts HDI for CO2 emissions per capita and material footprint, capturing pressure on future generations.

q.s: The National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) was launched in:
q.x: NSAP began in 1995; the National Extension Service came in 1953 and MGNREGA in 2005.

q.s: Which section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 amended Article 371D to cover both Andhra Pradesh and Telangana?
q.x: Section 97 amended Article 371D; Section 96 provided Telangana with a Legislative Council under Article 168.

q.s: Under the Current Weekly Status (CWS), a person is counted as employed if he worked for at least:
o: One hour on any day of the reference week
q.x: The one-hour threshold under CWS means very little work counts as employment, so underemployment can be masked.

q.s: The First Finance Commission of India (1951) was chaired by:
q.x: K.C. Neogy headed the First Finance Commission; K. Santhanam headed the Second.

q.s: The Antyodaya programme began in 1977-78 in which State?
q.x: Antyodaya started in Rajasthan; the UNDP's first HDR (1990) was led by Mahbub ul Haq of Pakistan.

q.s: Inclusive growth looks at:
o: Both the pace and the pattern of growth
q.x: Inclusive growth focuses on both how fast and how broadly growth occurs, targeting marginal farmers, landless labourers and SC/ST communities.

q.s: NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index is computed using which method?
q.x: The National MPI uses the Alkire-Foster method with technical inputs from OPHI and UNDP.

q.s: Which two indicators does the National MPI add to the ten indicators of the Global MPI?
q.x: The National MPI has 12 indicators, adding maternal health and bank account.

q.s: The ten guiding principles of Andhra Pradesh's Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 are called:
q.x: Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 rests on ten principles, the 'Padi Sutralu'; Navaratnalu was the earlier welfare package.

q.s: The National Renewal Fund (1992) was set up to:
o: Protect workers affected by industrial restructuring
q.x: The NRF was a safety net for workers in sick and loss-making units after the 1991 industrial policy.

q.s: Under which Article does the Governor constitute a State Finance Commission every five years?
q.x: Article 243-I provides for the SFC; Article 243Y makes the same SFC review municipal finances.

q.s: The Twelfth Schedule lists how many subjects for municipalities?
q.x: The Twelfth Schedule (Article 243W) has 18 subjects; the Eleventh Schedule for panchayats has 29.

q.s: In the Union Budget 2026-27, which is the largest source of the Centre's rupee?
q.x: Borrowings and other liabilities make up 24 paise; income tax 21 paise and corporation tax 18 paise.

q.s: A national Goods and Services Tax was first proposed by:
o: Vijay Kelkar Committee on Direct Taxes (2002)
q.x: The Kelkar Task Force on implementation of the FRBM Act (2004) first proposed a national GST.

q.s: In 2024, India's share in world commercial services exports was about:
q.x: India's services export share rose from about 2 per cent in 2005 to 4.3 per cent in 2024.

q.s: Which was India's largest single export item in 2024-25?
q.x: Petroleum products led India's exports in 2024-25; electronics exports rose to about $38.56 billion, mostly smartphones.

q.s: NIRVIK, a scheme offering exporters higher insurance cover at lower premium, is run by:
q.x: NIRVIK (Niryat Rin Vikas Yojana) is an ECGC scheme; pre-shipment inspection is the Export Inspection Council's job.

q.s: Devaluation of a currency makes a country's:
q.x: Devaluation cheapens exports and raises the cost of imports, but it does not necessarily improve the trade balance.

q.s: The 'Mera Ration' app under One Nation One Ration Card was developed by DFPD with:
q.x: The Department of Food and Public Distribution developed Mera Ration with the National Informatics Centre; ONORC runs on IM-PDS.

q.s: The Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) was introduced in:
q.x: TPDS came in 1997, after the Revamped PDS (1992); the NFSA followed in 2013.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming (APCNF) is implemented by:
q.x: APCNF is run by Rythu Sadhikara Samstha and won the Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity 2024.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, pesticide use between 2014-15 and 2024-25:
o: Rose from about 1,716 MT to 2,650 MT
Fell from about 2,650 MT to 1,716 MT
q.x: Pesticide use in AP declined from about 2,650 MT to 1,716 MT, in line with the push for natural farming.

q.s: The first Krishi Vigyan Kendra was set up in 1974 at:
q.x: The first KVK was set up at Puducherry in 1974; Kisan Call Centres began in 2004 and ATMA in 2005.

q.s: MGNREGA guarantees how many days of wage employment per rural household in a year?
q.x: MGNREGA guarantees 100 days of work per household; wages are due within 15 days and one-third of beneficiaries should be women.

q.s: Under MGNREGA, what share of the beneficiaries should be women?
q.x: The Act requires that at least one-third of the beneficiaries be women.

q.s: Priority Sector Lending Certificates allow a bank to:
o: Borrow from the RBI at a lower rate
Meet its PSL shortfall by buying certificates
q.x: A bank short of its PSL target can buy PSLCs from banks that have exceeded theirs.

q.s: In November 2020, which State became the first to fix floor prices for vegetables?
q.x: Kerala fixed floor prices for 16 vegetables in November 2020.

q.s: The Price Stabilisation Fund (2015) maintains buffer stocks of:
q.x: The PSF builds buffers of onion, potato and pulses to check price volatility.

q.s: 'Anna Darpan' is a system meant to modernise the supply chain of:
q.x: Anna Darpan is FCI's supply-chain management system; under OMSS (Domestic) FCI sells central pool grain in the open market.

q.s: IM-PDS (Integrated Management of PDS), from April 2018, enabled:
o: Direct cash transfer of food subsidy
q.x: IM-PDS provided the platform for national portability under One Nation One Ration Card.

q.s: The National Manufacturing Policy, 2011 aimed to raise the share of manufacturing in GDP to:
q.x: The NMP aimed at 25 per cent by 2022 and 100 million jobs, but manufacturing stayed near 15-17 per cent of GVA.

q.s: MSME Samadhaan addresses which problem of MSMEs?
q.x: MSME Samadhaan is a portal for MSMEs to file cases of delayed payments by buyers.

q.s: District Industries Centres (DICs) were created by the Industrial Policy of 1977 to support:
q.x: The 1977 policy, drafted largely by George Fernandes, set up DICs as one-roof support for small and cottage industries.

q.s: Under the National Manufacturing Policy, 2011, the 100 million additional jobs were to be created in:
q.x: The NMP aimed to raise manufacturing to 25 per cent of GDP and create 100 million manufacturing jobs within a decade.

q.s: How many sectors did the original Make in India campaign (2014) cover?
q.x: Make in India began with 25 sectors; Make in India 2.0 covers 27 (15 manufacturing and 12 services).

q.s: The Guarantee Redemption Fund of a State is used to:
q.x: The Guarantee Redemption Fund meets invoked guarantees; the Consolidated Sinking Fund amortises liabilities.

q.s: What share of the divisible pool did the 15th Finance Commission recommend for the States?
q.x: The 14th FC fixed 42 per cent; the 15th set 41 per cent after J&K became a UT.

q.s: The backward districts package for Andhra Pradesh covers how many districts?
q.x: It covers the four Rayalaseema districts and three North Coastal districts, modelled on the KBK and Bundelkhand packages.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT among the Rayalaseema districts covered by the backward districts package?
q.x: The four Rayalaseema districts were Anantapur, Kurnool, YSR Kadapa and Chittoor.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming (APCNF) is implemented by:
q.x: APCNF is run by Rythu Sadhikara Samstha, a not-for-profit set up by the State Government.

q.s: Operation Greens covers which crops?
q.x: Operation Greens, modelled on Operation Flood, began with the TOP crops.

q.s: Which body supports PACS as Multi-Service Centres?
q.x: NABARD supports PACS as Multi-Service Centres; model bye-laws allow PACS over 25 non-credit activities.

q.s: The farmers' market concept of Rythu Bazars was first tried in Punjab under the name:
q.x: Punjab's Apni Mandi came first; Andhra Pradesh was the second State, with Rythu Bazars where farmers sell directly to consumers.

q.s: The Pattiseema lift irrigation scheme links which two rivers?
q.x: Pattiseema, working since 2015, lifts Godavari water into the Polavaram Right Main Canal to the Krishna.

q.s: The Prakasam Barrage at Vijayawada replaced the anicut built by:
q.x: The barrage replaced the 1850s Krishna anicut associated with Arthur Cotton; Nagarjuna Sagar is a large masonry dam.

q.s: The Telugu Ganga project supplies Krishna water mainly for the drinking needs of:
q.x: Telugu Ganga carries Krishna water via Srisailam, Somasila and Kandaleru to Poondi for Chennai.

q.s: Which of the following is a Propelling sector under Andhra Pradesh's IDP 4.0 (2024-29)?
q.x: IDP 4.0 has 10 Sustenance and 10 Propelling sectors; blue economy is Propelling, textiles a Sustenance sector.

q.s: The ONGC mini-refinery in Andhra Pradesh is located at:
q.x: ONGC's mini-refinery is at Tatipaka (Konaseema); HPCL's refinery is at Visakhapatnam and BPCL's proposed complex at Ramayapatnam.

q.s: The present Vijayawada-based APCPDCL was carved out in 2020 from:
q.x: APCPDCL was formed in 2020 from APSPDCL; the Hyderabad-based CPDCL of 2000 went to Telangana.

q.s: ULPIN, also called 'Bhu-Aadhaar', is a unique ID for:
q.x: ULPIN is a 14-digit alphanumeric land parcel ID based on the geo-coordinates of the parcel's vertices.

q.s: NGDRS under the land records programme is known as:
q.x: The National Generic Document Registration System is a common registration application, 'One Nation One Registration Software'.

q.s: Which of the following belongs to the organised money market in India?
q.x: Commercial banks are part of the organised market controlled by the RBI; moneylenders, indigenous bankers, chit funds and nidhis form the unorganised market.

q.s: Which is the outermost of the major layers of the Sun?
q.x: From the inside out: core, radiative zone, convective zone, photosphere, chromosphere and corona.

q.s: The Coriolis force is maximum at the:
q.x: The Coriolis force is zero at the Equator, increases with latitude and is maximum at the poles; it also increases with wind speed.

q.s: How many Indian States does the Tropic of Cancer pass through?
q.x: The Tropic of Cancer crosses eight States, from Gujarat in the west to Mizoram in the east.

q.s: Uttarayana refers to the Sun's apparent movement:
q.x: Uttarayana is the apparent northward movement after the winter solstice; the southward movement is Dakshinayana.

q.s: Which seismic waves cannot pass through liquids?
q.x: S-waves are transverse and travel only through solids, which is why they reveal the liquid outer core; P-waves arrive first.

q.s: Which scale is preferred for measuring large earthquakes?
q.x: The Moment Magnitude (Mw) scale, based on fault rupture area and slip, is used for large earthquakes; Mercalli and MSK-64 measure intensity.

q.s: Which is the highest peak of Europe?
q.x: Elbrus in the Caucasus is the highest in Europe; Mont Blanc is the highest in the Alps.

q.s: Mount Aconcagua, the highest peak outside Asia, is located in:
q.x: Aconcagua (6,961 m) in the Andes of Argentina is the highest peak of South America.

q.s: Juba is the capital of which landlocked African country?
q.x: Juba is the capital of South Sudan, independent since 2011.

q.s: After the 2023-24 remeasurement, the length of India's coastline is about:
q.x: The remeasured coastline is 11,098.81 km, up from the earlier 7,516.6 km.

q.s: Which Indian State faces the most cyclone disasters?
q.x: The east coast is more cyclone-prone than the west, and Odisha faces the most cyclone disasters.

q.s: El Nino is an abnormally warm ocean current that replaces which cold current off Peru?
q.x: El Nino replaces the cold Humboldt current off Peru and Ecuador around Christmas and recurs every 2-7 years.

q.s: The troposphere is thickest over the:
q.x: The troposphere extends to about 18 km over the equator and about 8 km over the poles, because of strong convection at the equator.

q.s: The normal lapse rate of temperature in the troposphere is about:
q.x: Temperature falls with height at about 6.5 degree C per km in the troposphere.

q.s: The most important cause of tsunamis is:
q.x: Most tsunamis are generated by vertical displacement of the sea floor in undersea earthquakes.

q.s: Which of the following States does NOT share a border with Karnataka?
q.x: Karnataka borders Goa, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala.

q.s: Which State lies to the west of the Rayalaseema region?
q.x: Rayalaseema has Karnataka to the west, Tamil Nadu to the south and Telangana to the north.

q.s: The Indian Standard Meridian is:
q.x: IST is based on 82 degree 30' E, which passes near Mirzapur; 82.5 x 4 minutes gives IST = GMT + 5:30.

q.s: Meghalaya receives very heavy rainfall mainly from:
o: Arabian Sea branch of the south-west monsoon
Bay of Bengal branch of the south-west monsoon
q.x: Bay of Bengal winds forced up the funnel-shaped Khasi hills give Mawsynram and Cherrapunji very heavy rain.

q.s: Which river valley is among the worst flood-affected regions of India?
q.x: The Brahmaputra valley in Assam suffers recurring severe floods.

q.s: In the northern plains of India, rainfall generally:
q.x: Rainfall falls from east to west, so Kolkata gets more than Patna and Delhi; in the peninsula it falls from west to east.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh receives the larger share of its annual rainfall from the:
q.x: About two-thirds of AP's rain comes from the south-west monsoon and one-third from the north-east monsoon.

q.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh receives the maximum north-east monsoon rainfall?
q.x: Nellore on the south coast gets the most north-east monsoon rain.

q.s: Loktak lake is located in:
q.x: Loktak, known for its floating phumdis, is in Manipur; Lonar is in Maharashtra and Roopkund in Uttarakhand.

q.s: The Narmada and the Tapi flow westwards through:
q.x: Both rivers flow west through trough faults (rift valleys) and form estuaries, not deltas.

q.s: The Handri-Neeva Sujala Sravanthi draws water from:
q.x: Handri-Neeva lifts Krishna water from the Srisailam backwaters for Kurnool, Anantapur, Kadapa and Chittoor.

q.s: The KC (Kurnool-Cuddapah) Canal takes off from:
q.x: The KC Canal starts at the Sunkesula barrage on the Tungabhadra and serves Kurnool and Kadapa.

q.s: Red soils owe their colour to:
q.x: Red soils are poor in humus; their colour comes from iron oxide, and they look yellow when hydrated.

q.s: Alpine forests in India occur in:
q.x: Alpine vegetation grows high in the Himalayas; coniferous forests occupy the temperate belt of about 1,500-3,000 m.

q.s: The State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) is trained by:
q.x: SDRFs draw on State police, fire services and home guards and are trained by the NDRF; they follow a battalion model.

q.s: The High Powered Committee on Disaster Management (1999) was chaired by:
q.x: The J.C. Pant committee was set up in August 1999; the National Policy on Disaster Management was approved in 2009.

q.s: Under the Disaster Management (Amendment) Act, 2025, an Urban Disaster Management Authority is headed by:
q.x: UDMAs in State capitals and corporation cities are headed by the Municipal Commissioner.

q.s: The Upper Ganga Canal takes off from:
q.x: The Upper Ganga Canal begins at Bhimgoda (Haridwar); the Lower Ganga Canal at Narora.

q.s: Which physiographic region of India is the country's mineral heartland?
q.x: The Peninsular plateau holds iron ore, coal, bauxite and mica; the alluvial plains have few minerals.

q.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh stands first in iron ore?
q.x: Anantapur leads in iron ore, mostly haematite; it also occurs in Kadapa, Prakasam and Krishna.

q.s: The aluminium industry is primarily located near sources of:
q.x: Smelting alumina needs large amounts of electricity, so aluminium plants are power-oriented.

q.s: National Investment and Manufacturing Zones (NIMZs) were introduced under the:
q.x: NIMZs were created under the NMP 2011 and are larger than SEZs.

q.s: Which canal is a sea-level canal without locks?
q.x: The Suez Canal (1869) has no locks; the Panama Canal (1914) uses a lock system.

q.s: Which State has the longest coastline in India?
q.x: Gujarat has the longest coastline, followed by Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.

q.s: Which country was India's top supplier of crude oil in 2025?
q.x: Russia has been India's largest crude supplier; India depends on imports for about 88-89 per cent of its crude.

q.s: According to Census 2011, which State had the lowest literacy rate?
q.x: Bihar had the lowest literacy rate (61.8 per cent) in 2011; Kerala the highest.

q.s: International Literacy Day, declared by UNESCO in 1966, is observed on:
q.x: International Literacy Day is observed on 8 September, first in 1967.

q.s: In higher education, female Gross Enrolment Ratio in India has risen to about:
q.x: Female GER in higher education rose to 30.2, exceeding the male GER.

q.s: According to Census 2011, which district of the then 13-district Andhra Pradesh had the lowest total literacy?
q.x: Vizianagaram had the lowest total literacy (58.89 per cent); West Godavari had the highest (74.32 per cent).

q.s: Under Article 342, the Scheduled Tribes of a State are notified by:
o: The Governor after consulting the President
The President after consulting the Governor
q.x: The President notifies STs after consulting the Governor; only Parliament can change the list.

q.s: According to Census 2011, which State had the largest number of census towns?
q.x: West Bengal had the most census towns; Goa (62.17 per cent) was the most urbanised major State.

q.s: The term 'Megalopolis' is associated with:
q.x: Gottmann (1961) used megalopolis for the north-eastern US seaboard; Geddes coined conurbation and Jefferson primate city.

q.s: The concept of 'conurbation' was introduced by:
q.x: Patrick Geddes coined conurbation for a continuous urban area formed by merging towns.

q.s: 'Adi Vaani', an AI translation platform, is meant for:
q.x: Adi Vaani, launched under the Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan, first covers Bhili, Gondi, Mundari and Santali.

q.s: According to Census 2011, which religious community had the highest sex ratio?
q.x: Christians had the highest sex ratio (about 1,023) and Sikhs the lowest among the six major communities.

q.s: The Centre of Excellence for Studies in Classical Telugu (CESCT) was moved to:
q.x: CESCT, a wing of the Central Institute of Indian Languages (Mysuru), was shifted to Nellore.

q.s: Standard modern Telugu is based mainly on the dialect of:
q.x: Standard Telugu rests on the central coastal Krishna-Godavari dialect.

q.s: What is the official language of Goa?
q.x: Konkani is Goa's official language, with Marathi also used for official purposes.

q.s: Coral reefs do not grow near muddy river mouths mainly because:
o: Corals need clean, sediment-free water of normal salinity
q.x: Freshwater and sediment at river mouths block light and lower salinity, preventing coral growth.

q.s: India's first national park, set up in 1936 as Hailey National Park, is now called:
q.x: Hailey National Park was renamed Corbett National Park; Madhya Pradesh has the most national parks.

q.s: Dachigam National Park is famous for the:
q.x: Dachigam near Srinagar is the home of the hangul (Kashmir stag); the Asiatic lion is in Gir.
